description: What a quiz client tells a learner about a pseudonym or name the handle policy refuses. The policy is the core's `normalizeHandle` (white space runs collapse to one space and are trimmed, U+2019 becomes an apostrophe; then 1 to 64 code points of Latin letters, ASCII digits, single spaces and ' . _ -, with at least one letter or digit; raw input over 256 code points is refused); the client first brings the typed text into NFC. A fault is the first that applies of: `characters` (the distinct refused characters in typed order), `empty` (nothing but white space), `long` (the length of the handle as it would be kept; the typed length when even that is over 256) and `letter` (no letter or digit). `fault` null means the core accepts the handle. Typed texts are given as code point lists so that no editor can change them.

refusals.description: A sign-up the proctor refuses although nothing is wrong with what the learner typed. (1) Its network (one client address) has spent its sign-up allowance: the proctor answers 429 with a body that names the allowance and the wait until the next single sign-up of that address. The client does not send the sign-up again by itself; it says what happened, that it passes by itself, after how many seconds (the wait rounded up to whole seconds, at least 1; no number when the proctor named no wait) to try again, and that continuing with an existing pseudonym works at once — recalling a pseudonym is a read, not a sign-up. Until the wait is over the client asks the proctor for no further sign-up and answers with the time that is left. A 429 that names no allowance, or one this client does not know, stays a shortage that is waited out silently. (2) The roster is full (rejection roster-full): waiting does not help; only the operator can raise the limit. Each vector is the failure the client holds and the sentence it shows in each language.

vectors.id: the sign-up allowance is spent and the proctor says for how long
vectors.en: Too many new learners have signed up from your network just now, so the quiz server takes no further sign-up from it for the moment. This passes by itself: try again in about 36 s – or continue with a pseudonym you already have, which works right away.
vectors.de: Aus deinem Netzwerk haben sich gerade sehr viele neu angemeldet, deshalb nimmt der Quiz-Server von dort im Moment keine weitere Anmeldung an. Das geht von selbst vorbei: Versuch es in etwa 36 s noch einmal – oder mach mit einem Pseudonym weiter, das du schon hast; das geht sofort.

vectors.en: The quiz server has reached its maximum number of learners and takes no new ones until its operator raises the limit; trying again does not help until then. You can continue with a pseudonym that already exists.
